scope: Adults with suspected or confirmed gout, using stored NICE NG219 recommendation text.

keyRecommendations.text: Suspect gout with rapid-onset severe pain, redness and swelling in one or both first MTP joints, or with tophi.
keyRecommendations.population: People presenting with acute joint symptoms

keyRecommendations.text: A serum urate of 360 micromol/L (6 mg/dL) or more supports the clinical diagnosis. If the level is lower during a flare and gout is strongly suspected, repeat it at least 2 weeks after the flare settles.
Offer an NSAID, colchicine, or a short course of oral corticosteroid for a flare, accounting for comorbidities and co-prescriptions.
Offer treat-to-target urate-lowering therapy for multiple or troublesome flares, CKD stages 3 to 5, diuretic therapy, tophi, or chronic gouty arthritis.

clinicalBottomLine: NG219 diagnoses gout from the clinical picture plus urate, treats the flare with an NSAID, colchicine, or a short oral corticosteroid, and uses treat-to-target urate lowering when high-risk features are present.
notableCaveats: Oral corticosteroids for flares were noted as off-label in June 2022. Colchicine dose and drug-interaction lists are not in the stored recommendation text.
